title: Read a selected value safely
prompt: A pointer may name an int or be null. Return the pointed-to value when present, otherwise return the caller’s fallback. Do not store the pointer or dereference null.
solution:
#include <iostream>

int selectedValue(const int* selected,int fallback){ return selected?*selected:fallback; }

tests.label: Present pointer
tests.hint: Read through the pointer only when nonnull.

tests.label: Zero is valid pointed value
tests.hint: Zero and absence are different states.

hints: Check a pointer before using * to read the object it points at.
explanation: The pointer borrows an object. The function neither owns nor retains it. The caller must keep that int alive for the duration of the call.
